==English== {{wp}} ===Pronunciation=== * {{a|en|UK}} ** {{enPR|tôk|a=RP}} {{IPA|en|/tɔːk/}} ** {{IPA|en|[tʰoːk]|a=SSBE,MLE}} *** {{audio|en|LL-Q1860 (eng)-Vealhurl-talk.wav|a=Southern England}} *** {{audio|en|En-uk-to talk.ogg|a=London|text=to talk}} ** {{IPA|en|/tɔk/|a=Scotland}} ** {{IPA|en|/taːk/|a=Northumbria}} * {{a|en|US|CA}} ** {{IPA|en|/tɔk/|a=GA,non-cot-caught}} *** {{audio|en|LL-Q1860 (eng)-Grendelkhan-talk.wav|a=Connecticut}} ** {{enPR|tŏk|a=GA,cot-caught,dialects of Canada}} {{IPA|en|/tɑk/|[tʰɑk]|[tʰäk]}} *** {{audio|en|en-us-talk.ogg|a=California}} ** {{IPA|en|/tɔʊ̯k/|a=AAVE}} ** {{IPA|en|/tɒk/|a=CA,dialects of the US}} * {{IPA|en|/toːk/|a=AU,NZ}} * {{homophones|en|torc|torq|torque>>|;|tock|aa4=cot-caught}} * {{rhymes|en|ɔːk|s=1}} ===Etymology 1=== {{ety|en|:inh|enm:talken>>>}} From {{inh|en|enm|talken}}, {{m|enm|talkien}}, from {{inh|en|ang|*tealcian|t=to talk, chat}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*talkōn}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*talkōną|t=to talk, chatter}}, frequentative form of {{der|en|gem-pro|*talōną|t=to count, recount, tell}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*dol-}}, {{m|ine-pro|*del-|t=to aim, calculate, adjust, count}}, equivalent to {{m|en|tell}} + {{m|en|-k}}. {{col-top|2|cog}} Cognate with {{cog|nds|taalken|t=to chatter, gossip, talk}}. Related also to {{cog|bar|zoin|t=to pay}}, {{cog|cim|zaln|t=to pay}}, {{cog|nl|talen|t=to care, long; to speak; to say}}, {{cog|de|zahlen|t=to pay}}, {{cog|mhn|zoln|t=to pay}}, {{cog|da,nb|tale|t=to talk, speak}}, {{cog|fo,is,sv|tala|t=to speak, talk}}, {{cog|nn|tala|t=to speak, talk}}; also {{cog|la|dolus|t=deceit, deception, fraud, guile, treachery, trickery; malice; artifice, device, stratagem}}, {{cog|grc|δόλος|t=deceit, trick; wiles; bait}}, {{cog|hy|տող|t=line (in a text)}}. More at {{l|en|tale}}. Despite the surface similarity, unrelated to {{noncog|ine-pro|*telkʷ-|t=to talk}} (due to Grimm's law), which is the source of {{m|en|loquacious}}. {{col-bottom}} ====Alternative forms==== * {{alter|en|talke|taulke||obsolete}} ====Verb==== {{en-verb}} # {{lb|en|intransitive}} To [[communicate]], usually by means of [[speech]]. #: {{ux|en|Let's sit down and '''talk'''.}} #: {{ux|en|Although I don't speak Chinese, I managed to '''talk''' with the villagers using signs and gestures.}} #* {{RQ:Shakespeare Merchant of Venice|I|iii|page=166|passage=I will buy with you, sell with you, '''talk''' with you, walk with you, and so following, but I will not eat with you.}} #* {{RQ:Lincoln Pratt's Patients|page=99|chapter=4|passage=Then he commenced to '''talk''', really '''talk'''. and inside of two flaps of a herring's fin he had me mesmerized, like Eben Holt's boy at the town hall show. He '''talked''' about the ills of humanity, and the glories of health and Nature and service and land knows what all. {{...}} It was a chance he was offering me, a wonderful, eighteen carat, solid gold chance.}} #* {{RQ:Allingham China Governess|chapter=5|passage=Mr. Campion appeared suitably impressed and she warmed to him. He was very easy to '''talk''' to with those long clown lines in his pale face, a natural goon, born rather too early she suspected.}} #* {{RQ:Maxwell Mirror and the Lamp|chapter=XXV|page=203|passage=“{{...}} They '''talk''' of you as if you were Croesus—and I expect the beggars sponge on you unconscionably.” And Vickers launched forth into a tirade very different from his platform utterances. He spoke with extreme contempt of the dense stupidity exhibited on all occasions by the working classes.}} # {{lb|en|transitive|informal}} To [[discuss]]; to talk about. #: {{ux|en|They sat down to '''talk''' business.}} #: {{ux|en|That's enough about work, let's '''talk''' holidays!}} # {{lb|en|transitive}} To speak (a certain language). #: {{ux|en|We '''talk''' French sometimes.}} # {{lb|en|transitive|informal|chiefly used in progressive tenses}} {{n-g|Used to emphasise the importance, size, complexity etc. of the thing mentioned.}} #: {{ux|en|Are you interested in the job? They're '''talking''' big money.}} #: {{ux|en|We're not '''talking''' rocket science here: it should be easy.}} # {{lb|en|intransitive|slang}} To [[confess]], especially implicating others. #: {{ux|en|Suppose he '''talks'''?}} #: {{ux|en|She can be relied upon not to '''talk.'''}} #: {{ux|en|They tried to make me '''talk.'''}} # {{lb|en|intransitive}} To criticize someone for something of which one is guilty oneself. #: {{ux|en|I am not the one to '''talk'''.}} #: {{ux|en|She is a fine one to '''talk'''.}} #: {{ux|en|You should '''talk'''.}} #: {{ux|en|Look who's '''talking'''.}} # {{lb|en|intransitive}} To [[gossip]]; to create [[scandal]]. #: {{ux|en|People will '''talk'''.}} #: {{ux|en|Aren't you afraid the neighbours will '''talk'''?}} # {{lb|en|transitive}} To manifest outwardly in speech, as opposed to reality or action. #* {{quote-journal|en|date=22 Dec 79|volume=2|number=22|journal=Gay Community News|page=5|author=S. J. Harris|title=Life And Spirit|text=Remember that Christ and Christianity may not always be the same thing; e.g. Jerry Falwell '''''talks''''' "Christianity" but practices hatred {{...}} which is diametrically opposed to what Jesus really taught.}} # {{lb|en|informal|chiefly used in progressive tenses}} To influence someone to express something, especially a particular [[stance]] or [[viewpoint]] or in a particular [[manner]]. #: {{ux|en|That's not like you at all, Jared. The drugs are '''talking'''. Snap out of it!}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=2013|author=Stephen Coonts|title=Fortunes of War |passage="So, are you going to give up all this good living and easy money and come fly for the Russians?"
"Hello no. I told you that yesterday."
"That was your wallet '''talking'''. The shooting has started. I found a condom in his room.}} ## {{lb|en|US}} A customary conversation in which the parent(s) of a [[black]] child explain the [[racism]] and [[violence]] they may face, especially when interacting with [[police]], and strategies to manage it. ##* {{quote-book|en|year=2012|author=Crystal McCrary|title=Inspiration: Profiles of Black Women Changing Our World|isbn=1613123442 |passage=Later, I made sure to have '''the talk''' with my son about being a black boy, {{...}}}} ##* {{quote-book|en|year=2016|author=Jim Wallis|title=America's Original Sin: Racism, White Privilege, and the Bridge|isbn=1493403486 |passage=All the black parents I have ever spoken to have had “'''the talk'''” with their sons and daughters. “'''The talk'''” is a conversation about how to behave and not to behave with police.}} ##* {{quote-book|en|year=2016|author=Stuart Scott; Larry Platt|title=Every Day I Fight|isbn=1101983175|page=36 |passage=Now, I was a black man in the South, and my folks had had “'''the talk'''” with me.
